Fasting for individuals with diabetes presents conflicting evidence and guidance. Some sources report potential benefits of intermittent fasting under careful medical supervision, including weight loss and reduced insulin requirements in small human studies [d1][d3]. However, multiple authoritative sources strongly caution against fasting for many people with diabetes due to risks such as hypoglycemia, poor glycemic control, and exacerbation of complications, especially during Ramadan [d6][d7]. Clinical reviews also note that intermittent fasting is not appropriate for those whose conditions require regular food intake because of medication effects, explicitly including diabetes [d2]. Given these divergent findings and safety concerns, individuals with diabetes should consult their healthcare providers before considering fasting [d1][d2][d4][d5].
